headline: RPI's own CPT page, confirmed again on a second direct read, has in fact dropped its post-guidance 'Spring 2027' restriction entirely — no SEVP guidance, BCM or court-ruling citation anywhere — making it, like Northwestern, a silent and unannounced reversion to the pre-August standard; a thirteenth full reversion, with existing-approval treatment still unstated. No other school changed tier. DHS, Tufts and Claremont McKenna tripwires unchanged; still no confirmed DHS appeal or CPT-specific Federal Register rulemaking.

tripwires.name: DHS SEVIS Help Hub CPT page
tripwires.detail: Re-confirmed 25 Nov 18:10 UTC — unchanged: "Last updated: August 24, 2026," no mention of the 17 Nov court ruling; only standard DSO cancel ("before the CPT start date")/edit ("after the CPT start date...can only edit...to shorten the CPT end date") rules, no language on students who already hold CPT authorization. The companion DHS CPT-guidance page, re-checked the same run, still only says SEVP 'plans to release' draft guidance, no ruling mention; page carries no update date at all, just a general 'this content may be outdated' caution.

tripwires.name: Tufts I-Center CPT page
tripwires.detail: Re-confirmed 25 Nov 18:10 UTC — unchanged, still says "the I-Center is unable to process CPT requests for non-required internships at this time"; no mention of the 17 Nov court ruling; no new language on already-authorised students.

tripwires.name: Federal Register rulemaking on CPT
tripwires.detail: RULING, 17 Nov 2026: US District Judge Julia Kobick (D. Mass.) granted the plaintiffs' motion for a preliminary injunction and stay of agency action in Association of American Universities et al. v. DHS, No. 1:26-cv-14520 — barring DHS from enforcing the Aug 12/24 SEVP CPT guidance, finding it likely arbitrary and capricious under the Administrative Procedure Act; per Dartmouth's own page, the stay bars enforcement "both prospectively and with respect to conduct and approvals that occurred prior to the issuance of the broadcasts." Not a final ruling; DHS may appeal and has declined to comment. Six schools have now fully reverted on their own pages: Buffalo, Alabama, UT Dallas, UC Berkeley, Middlebury and, newly this run, George Washington — whose ISO posted "Important Update: Federal Court Blocks SEVP CPT Guidance & Clarifications on Institutional CPT Policy" (18 Nov), stating the ruling "protects both future and past CPT approvals" and that it will again authorise CPT tied to an elective course ("It can be an elective course that you choose to take"), not only one required for graduation; already-approved students "do not need to take any action." Middlebury's ISSS page carries a 17 Nov banner saying Winter Term 2027 CPT applications are 'NOW OPEN...as a result of the court ruling,' the first evidence Middlebury had any CPT pause at all (it was previously 'clear', with no restriction ever found; the original pause's cause and dates are not stated). Penn's ISSS Executive Director separately told the Daily Pennsylvanian (18 Nov email) that ISSS 'will not apply' the mandatory-for-all requirement while the court's order stands — a step toward reversal — but Penn's own page (dateModified 18 Nov) still only says 'Penn is covered by the court's order' with no processing change described, so not counted as a reversion yet. Columbia, U Washington, UC San Diego, Boston University, Michigan, UC Irvine report no processing change yet; a search-engine paraphrase of Columbia's own isso.columbia.edu pages (four distinct URLs now 403'd to direct fetch, including a second news post tried this run) still suggests Columbia 'will resume consideration of applications for elective CPT' — unconfirmed by a verbatim read, re-verify next run. The Harvard Crimson (19 Nov) separately reports Harvard 'has not updated its CPT guidance' since the ruling. UIUC and Washington University in St. Louis describe more active, narrower resumption paths short of full reversion (WashU pending a new CPT-eligible course list due 30 Nov). William & Mary and U Washington acknowledge the ruling without changing processing, joining the six-plus-school cautious group. Georgetown's own CPT page (internationalservices.georgetown.edu/students/employment/cpt/) newly acknowledges the 17 Nov pause directly on 21 Nov, says Georgetown is reviewing its F-1 CPT policy and 'will communicate any updates to student eligibility by December 1' — an eighth school in the acknowledging-without-change cohort; existing-approval treatment still not stated. University of Minnesota's own ISSS page (isss.umn.edu/fstudents/employment/cpt, updated 18 Nov) newly reports a full reversion: following the 17 Nov stay, ISSS 'will resume processing both required and elective CPT experiences,' with the MyISSS CPT request form reopening 23 Nov — a seventh full reversion, after Buffalo, Alabama, UT Dallas, Berkeley, Middlebury and George Washington. DHS's own SEVIS Help Hub and CPT-guidance tripwire pages, re-confirmed 22 Nov 12:11 UTC, still not updated to reflect the ruling, and the CPT-guidance page still only says SEVP 'plans to release' draft guidance; no confirmed DHS appeal filing of the CPT ruling yet; now seven full reversions (Buffalo, Alabama, UT Dallas, Berkeley, Middlebury, George Washington, Minnesota). Re-checked 22 Nov 18:09 UTC: DHS's own SEVIS Help Hub and CPT-guidance tripwire pages still unchanged, no ruling mention. Cornell's own alert page (international.globallearning.cornell.edu/alerts/cpt-applications-reopening-november-20, posted 20 Nov) frames the 17 Nov stay as 'only a temporary pause,' reopening CPT from 20 Nov for just three categories of 'previously eligible applicants' — Engineering Co-op, credit-bearing curriculum courses, PhD dissertation research needing outside resources — not a full reversion; degree-required CPT was already unaffected throughout. Columbia's own student paper, the Columbia Daily Spectator (19 Nov), headlines 'Columbia to resume review of international student work authorization applications' post-ruling, corroborating but not detailing the standing elective-CPT claim (isso.columbia.edu still 403's). A Yale Daily News headline ('Yale resumes approving foreign student summer work after court ruling') similarly reports a resumption; the article 429'd to direct fetch a third time (23 Nov); a search-engine paraphrase (not verbatim) says Yale will again consider elective CPT for credit, while Yale's own OISS page is unchanged. Neither Columbia's nor Yale's claim is confirmed by a direct read of the school's own page; both re-verify next run. University of Pittsburgh's own OIS page (ois.pitt.edu/curricular-practical-training), re-verified 23 Nov, now says CPT policies 'that were in effect prior to August 2026 will resume' and that 'the August 2026 guidance from SEVP is no longer applicable or in effect' — an eighth full reversion, after Buffalo, Alabama, UT Dallas, Berkeley, Middlebury, George Washington and Minnesota; existing-approval treatment not stated. DHS's own SEVIS Help Hub and CPT-guidance tripwire pages, re-confirmed 23 Nov 00:09 UTC, still not updated to reflect the ruling; no confirmed DHS appeal filing yet. Re-checked 23 Nov 06:10 UTC: DHS's tripwire pages still unchanged, no ruling mention; a fifth isso.columbia.edu URL (news/important-updates-cpt-opt-duration-status) also 403'd — Columbia's and Yale's reported resumptions remain unconfirmed by a direct read. Re-checked 23 Nov 12:12 UTC: DHS's tripwire pages still unchanged, no ruling mention, no confirmed DHS appeal. Northwestern's own OISS CPT page (updated 11/19) newly confirmed a ninth full reversion — no longer citing the Aug 2026 guidance or a mandatory-for-all standard, back to the pre-guidance eligibility standard — unlike the other eight, unannounced and not tied to the ruling by name. Yale's own site (oiss.yale.edu/immigration/immigration-changes), fetched directly for the first time, states 'the August restrictions are currently blocked' and that the 17 Nov injunction covers 'both future activity and earlier approvals' — the first direct confirmation on Yale's own page of the injunction's effect, though it stops short of confirming elective CPT processing has resumed. A sixth isso.columbia.edu URL (news/court-orders-injunction-and-stay-federal-cpt-advisories) also 403'd; Columbia's reported resumption remains unconfirmed by a direct read. Re-checked 23 Nov 18:09 UTC: DHS's tripwire pages still unchanged, no ruling mention, no confirmed DHS appeal; still nine full reversions (no tenth this run). Re-checked 24 Nov 00:09 UTC: DHS's tripwire pages still unchanged, no ruling mention, no confirmed DHS appeal; still nine full reversions. University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center's own new page (immigration-updates/blocks-cpt-restrictions.html), confirmed by direct fetch 24 Nov 06:09 UTC, says OIA 'has resumed processing CPT requests under the standards in place before the August 2026 broadcasts' following a court order that 'temporarily blocked nationwide' those restrictions — a tenth full reversion (after Buffalo, Alabama, UT Dallas, Berkeley, Middlebury, George Washington, Minnesota, Pittsburgh, Northwestern), though the page is undated and doesn't name the 17 Nov ruling. Re-checked 24 Nov 06:09 UTC: DHS's SEVIS Help Hub and CPT-guidance tripwire pages still unchanged, no ruling mention, no confirmed DHS appeal. Re-checked 24 Nov 12:14 UTC: DHS's tripwire pages still unchanged, no ruling mention, no confirmed DHS appeal; still ten full reversions (no eleventh this run). American University newly found via the .edu sweep — its own CPT page narrows new CPT to exclude elective-only internships, citing the 2026 SEVP guidance, but explicitly says students already approved for the current semester may continue; added to 'honored.' Re-checked 24 Nov 18:09 UTC: DHS's SEVIS Help Hub and CPT-guidance tripwire pages still unchanged, no ruling mention, no confirmed DHS appeal. Ohio State's own Immigration Updates page (oia.osu.edu, last updated 20 Nov 1:36pm) newly confirms the 17 Nov injunction and lists as its 'Action taken' that the CPT webpage was updated 'to policies in place prior to August 2026'; the CPT FAQ page itself no longer states a mandatory-for-all-students standard, though an unreconciled sentence elsewhere on the same Immigration Updates page still cites that stricter standard as the August guidance — an eleventh full reversion (after Buffalo, Alabama, UT Dallas, Berkeley, Middlebury, George Washington, Minnesota, Pittsburgh, Northwestern, UT Southwestern); existing-approval treatment not addressed. Re-checked 25 Nov 00:09 UTC: DHS's SEVIS Help Hub and CPT-guidance tripwire pages still unchanged, no ruling mention, no confirmed DHS appeal; still eleven full reversions (no twelfth this run). Yale's own OISS news page (oiss.yale.edu/news/federal-court-pauses-sevps-august-2026-cpt-guidance, dated 19 Nov), directly fetched for the first time 25 Nov 06:09 UTC, says 'effective today, OISS will again consider CPT requests for elective training taken for academic credit' following the 17 Nov injunction, superseding Yale's own standing CPT-update page which still states the required-of-all-students standard; already-authorised CPT 'nothing changes...remains valid' — a twelfth full reversion (after Buffalo, Alabama, UT Dallas, Berkeley, Middlebury, George Washington, Minnesota, Pittsburgh, Northwestern, UT Southwestern, Ohio State); students whose requests went unprocessed after 24 Aug must resubmit, not reversed automatically. Re-checked 25 Nov 06:09 UTC: DHS's SEVIS Help Hub and CPT-guidance tripwire pages still unchanged, no ruling mention, no confirmed DHS appeal or Federal Register rulemaking. Re-checked 25 Nov 12:10 UTC: DHS's tripwire pages still unchanged, no ruling mention, no confirmed DHS appeal or Federal Register rulemaking; MIT's own ISO page (iso.mit.edu), fetched directly for the first time, newly acknowledges the 17 Nov injunction — "MIT is currently reviewing the order" and will notify the community of policy updates "as soon as they become available" — the first of the four original 'cancels'-tier schools (Davidson, MIT, Skidmore, USF) to respond to the ruling on its own page, though it states no change to MIT's existing CPT cancellations. Re-checked 25 Nov 18:10 UTC: DHS's tripwire pages still unchanged, no ruling mention, no confirmed DHS appeal or Federal Register rulemaking; RPI's own page (isss.rpi.edu/resources/employment-us), re-confirmed on a second direct read, still shows no 'Spring 2027' restriction and no SEVP-guidance or ruling citation anywhere — moved from 'unstated' to 'clear' as a thirteenth full reversion, silent and unannounced like Northwestern's.

tripwires.name: Retroactive cancellation spreading
tripwires.detail: Tripped again 25 Nov 06:09 UTC — University of Massachusetts Amherst newly found via the .edu sweep on its own Global Affairs CPT page: students whose CPT was rescinded under the August SEVP guidance 'are not able to resume those activities for the remainder of the fall semester,' even after the 17 Nov injunction (new/future CPT requests may proceed again). A fifth confirmed interruption of already-granted CPT, after Davidson, MIT, Skidmore and University of South Florida — and the first of the five shown to persist despite the court order, rather than being an open question of temporariness. Re-checked 25 Nov 12:10 UTC: no additional school found with an already-granted-CPT cancellation; still five (Davidson, MIT, Skidmore, USF, UMass Amherst). MIT's own page newly acknowledges the 17 Nov injunction (see the Federal Register/litigation tripwire) but states no reversal of its cancellations yet. Re-checked 25 Nov 18:10 UTC: no additional school found with an already-granted-CPT cancellation; still five.

tiers.label: Already-approved CPT stopped or withdrawn
tiers.sub: The most severe response: students who already held an authorisation were told to stop work, or had it withdrawn.

schools.name: Davidson
schools.note: 15 Aug — paused new CPT and cancelled approved Fall 2026 authorisations after consulting counsel

schools.name: MIT
schools.note: paused new CPT incl. Professional Practice Requirement internships; contacting approved Fall 2026 students re alternatives. 25 Nov: ISO's page acknowledges 17 Nov injunction, says MIT reviewing, will notify of updates; no reversal yet

schools.name: Skidmore
schools.note: verified 15 Sept on Skidmore's own visa-employment page — CPT paused since the 12 Aug guidance, and students whose CPT was already authorised are told to stop work and await individual review, not continue. Not described as permanent.

schools.name: University of South Florida
schools.note: verified 29 Sept via its own paper, The Oracle — OIS revoked a student's already-approved, already-started CPT (approved 12 Aug, began working 24 Aug) a week later as not required for her degree; OIS's Sept update confirms stricter review.

schools.name: University of Massachusetts Amherst
schools.note: newly found 25 Nov via the .edu sweep on Global Affairs' own CPT page (umass.edu) — students whose CPT was rescinded under the August SEVP guidance 'are not able to resume those activities for the remainder of the fall semester,' even after the 17 Nov injunction; new/future CPT requests may proceed again, but the fall rescission itself stands — the first of the five cancellations confirmed to survive the court order.

tiers.label: Restricted — existing authorisations honoured
tiers.sub: New non-required CPT stopped; what was already approved stands.

schools.name: Columbia
schools.note: required-of-all + cooperative agreement only; pre-24 Aug approvals kept. 17 Nov ISSO post acknowledges the injunction/stay. isso.columbia.edu still 403's to direct fetch; a search-engine paraphrase suggests elective CPT review resuming, unconfirmed by a verbatim read. 22 Nov: Columbia's own paper, the Columbia Daily Spectator (19 Nov), headlines 'Columbia to resume review of international student work authorization applications' post-ruling — corroborates but doesn't detail elective-CPT or existing-approval treatment; still unconfirmed. 23 Nov: a sixth isso.columbia.edu URL (news/court-orders-injunction-and-stay-federal-cpt-advisories) also 403'd; still unconfirmed, re-verify directly

schools.name: Cornell
schools.note: updated 22 Nov on Cornell's own alert page (international.globallearning.cornell.edu/alerts/cpt-applications-reopening-november-20, posted 20 Nov) — post-17 Nov stay, CPT reopens 20 Nov only for 'previously eligible applicants': Engineering Co-op, credit-bearing curriculum courses, and PhD dissertation research needing outside resources; calls the stay 'only a temporary pause,' unlikely to apply retroactively if it survives; degree-required CPT 'unaffected' throughout; already-issued CPT not rescinded (per 25 Sept)

schools.name: USC
schools.note: mandatory-only; existing honoured

schools.name: American University
schools.note: found 24 Nov via the .edu sweep on ISSS's own CPT page (american.edu) — citing SEVP's 2026 guidance, ISSS will not process CPT requests based solely on an elective/optional internship, effective immediately; students already approved for the current semester may continue under their current I-20

schools.name: UC San Diego
schools.note: future processing suspended; existing fall authorisations honoured; updated 18 Nov on ISEO's own Immigration Policy Updates page (updated 11/17/2026) — aware of the preliminary injunction, consulting Legal Counsel/UCOP/peer institutions, 'unable to respond to individual questions' while reviewing; no decision yet, tier unchanged

schools.name: Santa Clara
schools.note: future processing suspended; existing fall authorisations honoured

schools.name: U Washington
schools.note: re-verified 20 Nov directly on ISS's own injunction post (iss.washington.edu/preliminary-injunction-cpt/, dated 17 Nov, updated 19 Nov) — 'for now, there are no changes and the CPT guidance for autumn quarter remains in effect' while ISS decides on winter/spring; already-authorized CPT continues per current I-20

schools.name: U Rochester
schools.note: 28 Aug — new non-required CPT paused, degree-required exception; already-approved CPT explicitly honoured

schools.name: UIUC
schools.note: re-verified 19 Nov on ISSS's own blog (blogs.illinois.edu/view/8569) — a 17 Nov post on the injunction says ISSS will resume issuing CPT that is integral to the curriculum, tied to a required class with a formal work component, or thesis-related, while the injunction is in place; a final ruling is still pending; existing-approval treatment not mentioned. Not a reversion to the pre-August standard; previously approved CPT not affected per the standing 24 Aug notice

schools.name: UC Davis

schools.name: U Michigan

schools.name: U Penn
schools.note: August halt, verified 9 Sept; current CPT authorisation continues through I-20 dates unless ISSS says otherwise. 17 Nov: ISSS's own CPT page (dateModified 18 Nov) still only says 'Penn is covered by the court's order,' no processing change described. 20 Nov, per the Daily Pennsylvanian (ISSS Executive Director's 18 Nov email): 'while the court's order remains in effect, ISSS will not apply the August broadcasts' requirement that practical training be mandatory for every student' — a step toward reversal not yet reflected on Penn's own page; tier held pending confirmation

schools.name: CU Boulder
schools.note: 20 Aug, verified 9 Sept on the ISSS FAQ — students already authorised for Fall 2026 CPT may continue their internship

schools.name: Duke

schools.name: Wesleyan

context: First CPT-specific litigation: on 5 Oct a coalition (AAU, Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration, NAFSA, AICUM) sued DHS in federal court in Massachusetts over the Aug 12/24 BCMs, calling them procedurally invalid and impermissibly retroactive; case is Association of American Universities et al. v. U.S. Department of Homeland Security et al., No. 1:26-cv-14520 (D. Mass.). After a 6 Nov hearing, US District Judge Julia Kobick ruled 17 Nov 2026, granting a preliminary injunction and stay of agency action barring DHS from enforcing the Aug 12/24 BCMs as likely arbitrary and capricious under the APA. Not a final ruling; DHS may appeal and has declined to comment. Schools are reacting unevenly to the ruling rather than uniformly reverting — thirteen (Buffalo, Alabama, UT Dallas, UC Berkeley, Middlebury, George Washington, Minnesota, Pittsburgh, Northwestern, UT Southwestern, Ohio State, Yale, RPI) have reverted to pre-August standards on their own pages as of 25 Nov, most citing the ruling but two (Northwestern, RPI) silently and without citing it; several more (U Washington, UC San Diego, Boston University, Columbia, Michigan, UC Irvine, Penn) are reviewing or have only acknowledged the ruling with no change yet; and DHS's own tripwire pages still have not been updated to reflect it. No third broadcast message. DHS's prior stated position: 'nothing about these regulations has changed.' ICE is auditing schools, with SEVP decertification as the stated risk. Immigration attorneys flag a retroactive-scrutiny risk — past CPT revisited at the OPT, STEM-OPT or H-1B stage. The common institutional reading of the pre-injunction standard: integral to the curriculum, required of all students in the programme for degree completion, a documented cooperative agreement with the employer, and DSO authorisation before training begins.

runs.summary: RPI's own page, confirmed on a second direct read, has in fact dropped its post-guidance 'Spring 2027' CPT restriction — no SEVP guidance, BCM or ruling citation anywhere — a thirteenth full reversion, silent and unannounced like Northwestern's; existing-approval treatment still unstated. No other school changed tier. DHS, Tufts, Claremont McKenna tripwires unchanged; no DHS appeal or Federal Register rulemaking found.

MIT's own page newly acknowledges the 17 Nov injunction, says it's reviewing the order — the first 'cancels'-tier school to respond, though no cancellation reversed. RPI's page quietly dropped its post-guidance 'Spring 2027' CPT restriction, unconfirmed either way. No school changed tier. DHS, Tufts, Claremont McKenna unchanged; no DHS appeal or Federal Register rulemaking found.

UMass Amherst newly found: a fifth school with already-granted CPT rescinded, and the first shown to keep that rescission in place even after the 17 Nov injunction (new requests may resume, the fall cancellation doesn't). Yale's own page now confirms elective CPT resumed — a twelfth full reversion. DHS, Tufts, Claremont McKenna unchanged.
